source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

govt_capex.evidence: Heavy reliance on Ministry of Defence orders (e.g. ₹295 crore and ₹177.5 crore simulator contracts from MoD in 2026); FY24 order book of ₹1,402 crore included ₹437 crore of exports to foreign defence/security agencies.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company reported as debt-free with cash and bank balances of approximately INR 1,217 crore.

inr_exposure.evidence: Company exposed to foreign currency risk on export revenue; secured export order worth over USD 41.5m for military training and counter-UAS solutions; targets $100M US revenue within three years.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: As part of the GSK multinational group, the India entity discloses imported vs indigenous raw/packing material consumption and net unhedged foreign currency exposure, and uses forward contracts to hedge currency/interest rate movements.
inr_exposure.evidence: Annual report discloses value of imported and indigenous raw and packing materials consumed, along with net unhedged exposure in currency; GSK group employs hedging techniques such as forwards for currency and interest rate movements.

rural.evidence: Company operates a pan-India sales network reaching over 60,000 retail outlets with emphasis on semi-urban and rural penetration.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Net debt was Rs 573.6 crore at end of FY25 (down further to Rs 244.1 crore by end of FY26); company has stated intent to actively reduce debt and become debt-free by FY27, implying meaningful bank borrowings/working capital debt exposed to interest rate movements, though floating-rate share was not disclosed in sources reviewed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Input costs for grain, ENA, glass and packaging remain volatile; industry commentary notes surging crude oil prices and a weaker rupee increasing import costs for packaging (glass bottles reported up ~20%, cartons up ~100% amid a Middle East geopolitical/crude spike).

inr_exposure.evidence: Company exports to 85-100+ countries; one source noted short-term export challenges due to US tariffs, implying some USD-linked export exposure, though no percentage was disclosed.

rural.evidence: Tractor segment (a key end-market Bosch supplies components to) grew 7.7% YoY in FY2024-25 aided by a favourable monsoon, higher MSPs and stepped-up rural infrastructure spending; two-wheeler segment grew 11.2% YoY helped by improved rural demand.

inr_exposure.evidence: Only ~8.3% of FY2024-25 sales were exports, mostly intercompany to other Bosch group entities; as a subsidiary of the German Bosch Group, currency exposure likely skews toward EUR rather than USD, but this was not confirmed in sources reviewed.

pli_scheme.evidence: A search-derived (unverified) source states Bosch Limited has been approved under the Component Champion Incentive Scheme of the PLI program for the automobile and auto components industry; this could not be corroborated against the company's own AR text in this session.

china_plus_one.evidence: Rising preference for Indian fluorochemical suppliers amid China+1 sentiment benefits NFIL's export-led business (analyst/broker commentary tied to Navin Fluorine's specialty chemicals and CDMO growth).
